mistakes.title: Vague, under-specified prompts
mistakes.body: Anthropic's golden rule is to show your prompt to a colleague with minimal context; if they would be confused, Claude will be too (Anthropic Docs — Prompting best practices, 2026).
mistakes.fix: State the task, audience, output format, and constraints explicitly before sending.

mistakes.title: Telling Claude what NOT to do
mistakes.body: Negative instructions ("Do not use markdown") are a documented failure mode; Claude responds better to positive direction (Anthropic Docs — "Control the format of responses").
mistakes.fix: Reframe as what TO do, e.g., "Your response should be composed of smoothly flowing prose paragraphs."

mistakes.title: Skipping few-shot examples
mistakes.body: Anthropic calls examples "one of the most reliable ways to steer Claude's output format, tone, and structure" and recommends 3–5 relevant, diverse examples in `<example>` tags (Anthropic Docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Add 3–5 canonical input/output pairs wrapped in `<examples>`.

mistakes.title: Stuffing edge cases into the prompt
mistakes.body: Anthropic's context-engineering guidance explicitly warns against a "laundry list" of edge-case examples; examples should be diverse and canonical, not exhaustive (Anthropic Engineering, Sept 2025).
mistakes.fix: Curate a small, representative example set and handle true edge cases in code or evals.

mistakes.title: Contradictory instructions left unresolved
mistakes.body: When a prompt contains conflicting rules, Claude will try to follow both, producing inconsistent output (Anthropic Docs — common failure modes).
mistakes.fix: Audit long system prompts for contradictions and rank rules by precedence.

mistakes.title: Brittle hardcoded if-else logic in system prompts
mistakes.body: Anthropic warns against both extremes: rigid if-else chains and vague high-level guidance; system prompts should sit at the "right altitude" (Anthropic Engineering — Effective context engineering).
mistakes.fix: Replace brittle branches with heuristics and clearly organized sections (`<instructions>`, `## Output description`).

mistakes.title: Aggressive "CRITICAL: You MUST…" tool-trigger language
mistakes.body: Prompts written to force tool use or stop "laziness" on older models cause overtriggering and overthinking on Claude 4.6+ models (Anthropic Docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Remove anti-undertrigger language when migrating to current models; describe the desired outcome instead.

mistakes.title: Writing your own step-by-step reasoning plan
mistakes.body: On current models, "prefer general instructions over prescriptive steps"; a prompt like "think thoroughly" often beats a hand-written reasoning chain (Anthropic Docs — Thinking and reasoning).
mistakes.fix: Give the goal and let adaptive thinking handle the reasoning; reserve manual CoT (`<thinking>`/`<answer>` tags) for when thinking is off.

mistakes.title: Mixing instructions, context, and data without delimiters
mistakes.body: Undifferentiated prompt blobs cause misinterpretation when prompts mix instructions, context, examples, and variable inputs (Anthropic Docs — Use XML tags).
mistakes.fix: Wrap each content type in its own tag (`<instructions>`, `<context>`, `<input>`) with consistent, descriptive names.

mistakes.title: Prompt engineering without success criteria or evals
mistakes.body: Anthropic's own guide assumes you already have clear success criteria, empirical tests, and a first-draft prompt; some failures are better fixed by changing the model or cost/latency tradeoff (Anthropic Docs — Prompt engineering overview).
mistakes.fix: Define measurable success criteria and a small eval set before iterating on wording.

mistakes.title: Putting the question before the document
mistakes.body: For 20k+ token inputs, queries placed at the END improve response quality by up to 30% in Anthropic's tests (Anthropic Docs — Long context prompting).
mistakes.fix: Put longform data at the top of the prompt; put the question last.

mistakes.title: Assuming the full context window is fully usable
mistakes.body: "Context rot" is documented: as tokens increase, recall degrades; treat context as a finite attention budget (Anthropic Engineering, Sept 2025).
mistakes.fix: Curate the smallest set of high-signal tokens; do not fill a 1M window just because it exists.

mistakes.title: Assuming every plan has a 1M-token window
mistakes.body: 1M tokens is standard on 5-series/4.6+ models, but Haiku 4.5 and consumer plans are 200K, and Claude Code defaults to 200K unless you opt in (Anthropic Docs, Jul 2026).
mistakes.fix: Check the model and surface before loading a large corpus.

mistakes.title: Not grounding answers in quotes on long documents
mistakes.body: Anthropic's documented anti-hallucination technique is to have Claude first extract relevant quotes (e.g., in `<scratchpad>` tags) and then answer (Anthropic prompt tutorial, Ch. 8).
mistakes.fix: Ask Claude to quote the relevant passages before performing the task.

mistakes.title: Using printed page numbers instead of viewer page numbers
mistakes.body: Anthropic's PDF guidance says to reference page numbers as shown in the PDF viewer, not the printed folios, which often differ (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Reference viewer page numbers when asking about specific pages.

mistakes.title: Letting one conversation run until quality collapses
mistakes.body: Anthropic's Claude Code guidance: if you've corrected Claude more than twice, run `/clear` and start fresh with a more specific prompt (Claude Code best practices).
mistakes.fix: Clear context between unrelated tasks and after repeated corrections.

mistakes.title: Ignoring compaction and note-taking strategies on long tasks
mistakes.body: Anthropic documents three long-horizon techniques — compaction, structured note-taking (NOTES.md / memory tool), and sub-agent architectures — for work that exceeds one window (Anthropic Engineering, Sept 2025).
mistakes.fix: Pick a strategy up front for multi-session work instead of hoping the window holds.

mistakes.title: Pre-loading everything instead of just-in-time retrieval
mistakes.body: Anthropic recommends lightweight identifiers (file paths, queries, links) and progressive disclosure over front-loading all context (Anthropic Engineering).
mistakes.fix: Give Claude pointers and let it retrieve what it needs.

mistakes.title: RAG-ing a knowledge base that fits in context
mistakes.body: Anthropic Engineering's own guidance: if your knowledge base is under ~200K tokens (~500 pages), include it whole with prompt caching instead of RAG (anthropic.com/engineering/contextual-retrieval).
mistakes.fix: Prefer full-context + prompt caching for small corpora.

mistakes.title: Ignoring ordering and formatting details
mistakes.body: Anthropic's tutorial notes Claude is more likely to pick the second of two options (ordering bias) and responds measurably worse to sloppy prompts (prompt tutorial; Simon Willison's notes).
mistakes.fix: Audit option order and proofread prompts — typos degrade results.

mistakes.title: Expecting visual analysis on a 150-page PDF
mistakes.body: Claude analyzes both text and visual elements (charts, images) only in PDFs of 100 pages or fewer; pages 101–1000 are processed text-only (support.claude.com — Upload files to Claude).
mistakes.fix: Split large PDFs into ≤100-page chunks when charts and figures matter.

mistakes.title: Uploading a PDF over 1000 pages
mistakes.body: PDFs over 1000 pages are rejected outright ("Uploaded file is too large") (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Split the document or upload sections separately.

mistakes.title: Uploading XLSX without enabling code execution
mistakes.body: XLSX uploads require the "code execution and file creation" feature to be enabled in your account (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Enable code execution and file creation before uploading spreadsheets.

mistakes.title: Trying to upload PPTX, ZIP, audio, or video
mistakes.body: The official supported-upload list does not include PowerPoint, ZIP, MP3/WAV, or MP4; PPTX is supported only as an output Claude creates (support.claude.com, Apr 2026).
mistakes.fix: Convert PPTX to PDF, unzip archives locally, and transcribe audio/video externally before uploading text.

mistakes.title: Believing the old 30MB chat upload limit
mistakes.body: Chat uploads were raised to **500 MB per file** (up to 20 files per chat) in 2026; older guides still cite 30MB — as of August 2026, verify current limits (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Re-check the upload article; note the code-execution sandbox itself still caps at 30MB per file (the two official pages conflict — flagged).

mistakes.title: Expecting embedded images in DOCX to be read
mistakes.body: Non-PDF documents get text extraction only; embedded images are not read (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Extract images and upload them separately as JPEG/PNG, or convert to PDF (≤100 pages).

mistakes.title: Uploading low-quality or tiny images
mistakes.body: Claude's documented vision limitations include errors on low-quality, rotated, or very small (<200px) images, and lossy JPEG compression hurts text legibility (platform.claude.com — Vision).
mistakes.fix: Use images ≥1000×1000 px, crop/straighten, and avoid heavy re-compression.

mistakes.title: Putting images after the text
mistakes.body: "Claude works best when images come before text" (Anthropic Docs — Vision).
mistakes.fix: Place images first, then the prompt; label multiple images ("Image 1:", "Image 2:").

mistakes.title: Asking Claude to identify people, judge AI-generated images, or do diagnostic scans
mistakes.body: Documented limitations: no person identification, cannot judge whether an image is AI-generated, approximate object counting, and not for CT/MRI-style diagnosis (platform.claude.com — Vision).
mistakes.fix: Design workflows around what vision supports; route identity/medical tasks elsewhere.

mistakes.title: Asking Claude to generate or edit raster images
mistakes.body: Claude does not generate or edit raster images (no text-to-image or inpainting); it produces SVG, Mermaid, charts, and code-based visuals instead (Anthropic Docs FAQ, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Ask for an SVG/diagram artifact, or connect an external generator via MCP.

mistakes.title: Expecting Projects on the Free plan
mistakes.body: Projects are a Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise feature; Free accounts do not get them (Anthropic — Projects, 2024-06-25; plan tables, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Upgrade, or use chat-level uploads and memory instead.

mistakes.title: Exceeding the 30MB project-file cap
mistakes.body: Project knowledge files are capped at 30MB each (vs 500MB chat uploads), with unlimited file count subject to the context window (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Split oversized files before adding them to project knowledge.

mistakes.title: Assuming RAG activates exactly at the context limit
mistakes.body: Officially, project RAG (project_knowledge_search) activates as content approaches the window limit, expanding capacity ~10x; but a reported bug (claude-code issue #25759, Feb 2026) shows RAG activating at ~13 files regardless of size — flagged discrepancy.
mistakes.fix: Verify retrieval quality empirically for your project size; don't assume the documented trigger.

mistakes.title: Putting images inside project documents expecting vision
mistakes.body: Project files get text extraction only (except multimodal PDFs), so images in DOCX knowledge files are invisible (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Use PDFs (≤100 pages) for knowledge that depends on figures.

mistakes.title: Treating project knowledge as a database, not context
mistakes.body: Total project content must fit the context window (or RAG's expanded ~10x capacity); it is retrieval into a finite window, not queryable storage (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Curate knowledge files; remove stale ones.

mistakes.title: Assuming shared-project chats are visible to teammates
mistakes.body: Chats inside shared projects are private by default; sharing is explicit (permission levels Private/View/Edit) (its.northeastern.edu, 2025).
mistakes.fix: Deliberately share chats into the project activity feed when collaboration is intended.

mistakes.title: Forgetting artifacts in projects aren't workspace-visible
mistakes.body: Artifacts created inside a project are shared only with project members, not the whole Team workspace (dim02 research, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Publish or export artifacts that need broader distribution.

mistakes.title: Not setting project custom instructions
mistakes.body: Projects support custom instructions; skipping them wastes the main benefit over plain chats (Anthropic — Projects).
mistakes.fix: Add role, style, and standing constraints to each project's instructions.

mistakes.title: Assuming memory sees everything equally
mistakes.body: Claude's cross-chat search respects project boundaries: chats outside projects vs within are treated separately (university IT documentation, 2025–2026).
mistakes.fix: Keep sensitive work inside projects; verify what memory can reference at Settings → Capabilities → Memory.

mistakes.title: Expecting memory to store transcripts
mistakes.body: Memory stores synthesized summaries (role, preferences, formatting), not full chat transcripts (Anthropic memory rollout, Mar 2026).
mistakes.fix: Put durable facts into project knowledge or say "add to memory…" explicitly for key items.

mistakes.title: Publishing an artifact assuming only your recipient can see it
mistakes.body: In July 2026, published artifacts and shared chats were indexed by Google due to a missing noindex directive (TechCrunch, 2026-07-27; remediated). Anthropic's position: share links "are not guessable or discoverable unless people choose to share them" — but the incident proves "unguessable" is not "private.".
mistakes.fix: Treat every publish/share link as potentially public; never include confidential data.

mistakes.title: Expecting attached files to travel with a shared chat
mistakes.body: Shared chats (claude.ai/share/…) are snapshots and attached files are excluded (Anthropic support docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Re-attach files in the receiving conversation or export them separately.

mistakes.title: Not revoking stale share links
mistakes.body: Share links persist until revoked; management lives at Settings → Privacy → Shared Chats (Anthropic support docs).
mistakes.fix: Periodically audit and revoke old links — a direct lesson of the July 2026 indexing incident.

mistakes.title: Using unsupported React patterns in artifacts
mistakes.body: Artifact React components require a default export, Tailwind core classes only, and a fixed library set (lucide-react, recharts, d3, Plotly, Three.js…); arbitrary npm imports fail (official system prompt constraints, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Design artifacts within the documented library set; external scripts only via cdnjs.

mistakes.title: Expecting artifacts to persist unlimited data
mistakes.body: Persistent artifact storage is capped at 20MB on paid plans (dim10 research, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Keep artifact state small; store large data in project files or externally.

mistakes.title: Confusing "Publish" with "Remix"
mistakes.body: Publish creates a public link; "Remix this Artifact" starts a NEW chat from someone else's published artifact — edits don't flow back (Anthropic artifacts documentation).
mistakes.fix: Use remix for reuse, publish for distribution; don't expect two-way sync.

mistakes.title: Expecting Live Artifacts everywhere
mistakes.body: Live Artifacts (refresh-on-open) launched April 2026 for paid plans in Cowork/Desktop contexts (dim10 research, 2026 — Medium-High confidence; verify availability).
mistakes.fix: Confirm your plan/surface supports Live Artifacts before designing dashboards around them.

mistakes.title: Sharing a chat that contains files uploaded for analysis
mistakes.body: Even though files are excluded from the share snapshot, quoted file content in the transcript is shared (behavior follows from §7 snapshot semantics).
mistakes.fix: Review the transcript for pasted confidential excerpts before sharing.

mistakes.title: Assuming artifact file creation works without the feature enabled
mistakes.body: Downloadable .docx/.pptx/.xlsx/.pdf output requires the "create files"/code-execution feature (a feature preview), enabled per account (support.claude.com, Apr 2026).
mistakes.fix: Enable code execution and file creation first; note Team/Enterprise network access is off by default in the sandbox.

mistakes.title: Treating shared links as access-controlled
mistakes.body: Share links carry no per-viewer authentication; anyone with the URL can view (implied by the July 2026 incident and Anthropic's "not guessable" statement).
mistakes.fix: For controlled distribution, share within projects/Team feeds with View/Edit permissions instead of public links.

mistakes.title: Repeating outdated model folklore
mistakes.body: Older claims (e.g., "200K context everywhere," "Opus is always best," stale benchmark percentages) lag the 2026 lineup: Fable 5, Opus 5 (GA 2026-07-24), Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5, invite-only Mythos 5 (cross-verified model research, Aug 2026).
mistakes.fix: Check the current model page before advising others — as of August 2026, verify against Anthropic's pricing/models docs.

mistakes.title: Sending `budget_tokens` to Claude 4.7+ models
mistakes.body: Manual extended thinking with `budget_tokens` is deprecated and returns a 400 error on Claude 4.7+; adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` + effort levels) replaced it (Anthropic Docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Migrate to adaptive thinking with `effort` (low→max) instead of a fixed thinking budget.

mistakes.title: Writing manual chain-of-thought prompts on adaptive-thinking models
mistakes.body: On current models, prescriptive "think step by step" scaffolding is a fallback for when thinking is OFF; Opus 5 thinks by default (Anthropic Docs — Thinking and reasoning).
mistakes.fix: Remove manual CoT boilerplate; use effort settings and, if needed, "think thoroughly."

mistakes.title: Carrying over verification boilerplate to Opus 5
mistakes.body: Anthropic documents that explicit verification instructions cause OVER-verification on Opus 5; remove them when migrating (Anthropic Docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Strip "verify your answer against X" instructions on Opus 5 unless you observe real failures.

mistakes.title: Using temperature folklore on 4.7+ models
mistakes.body: Older advice to crank temperature up/down for "creativity" predates adaptive-thinking 4.7+/5-series models, where behavior is steered primarily via prompts and the effort ladder (Anthropic Docs, 2026; flagged as evolving guidance).
mistakes.fix: Steer with explicit instructions and effort level; treat temperature tweaks as a last resort and test empirically.

mistakes.title: Using prefilled assistant responses on Claude 4.6+
mistakes.body: Prefill (putting words in Claude's mouth to force JSON) is no longer supported from Claude 4.6 onward — it returns a 400 error (Anthropic Docs — Migrating away from prefilled responses).
mistakes.fix: Use Structured Outputs (GA) for forced JSON/YAML, or system instructions ("Respond directly without preamble").

mistakes.title: Setting `max` effort everywhere
mistakes.body: Anthropic's own guidance: `max` can overthink; `xhigh` is recommended for coding/agentic work, minimum `high` for intelligence-sensitive tasks (Anthropic Docs — Prompting Claude Opus 4.7).
mistakes.fix: Right-size effort; raise it only if you observe shallow reasoning at lower settings.

mistakes.title: Using the word "think" on Opus 4.5 with thinking disabled
mistakes.body: Opus 4.5 (thinking off) is documented as sensitive to the word "think"; use "consider," "evaluate," or "reason through" instead (Anthropic Docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Reword thinking-trigger language when targeting that model configuration.

mistakes.title: Ignoring the Sonnet 5 pricing change
mistakes.body: Sonnet 5 intro pricing ($2/$10 per MTok) steps up to $3/$15 on 2026-09-01 — as of August 2026, verify current rates (Anthropic pricing, flagged).
mistakes.fix: Re-cost workloads before September 2026 budgets lock.

mistakes.title: Assuming long context costs extra
mistakes.body: The 1M-token window has been GA at standard pricing since March 2026 (no long-context surcharge) on supported models (Anthropic Docs).
mistakes.fix: Don't artificially chunk workloads to avoid a surcharge that no longer exists — but still respect context rot (Mistake 12).

mistakes.title: Assuming Claude gains permissions you don't have
mistakes.body: Effective connector permission is the intersection of the user's source-system permissions, OAuth scopes granted, MCP tool design, and Claude-side admin controls; Claude never gets broader access than the connecting user (technovids/Sunpeak connector guides, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Audit the intersection, not just the connector toggle — a read-only user stays read-only.

mistakes.title: Expecting Gmail to send email
mistakes.body: The Google connector is draft-only: "Claude creates drafts in your Gmail account, but cannot send emails on your behalf," and Gmail attachments aren't readable (Anthropic documentation, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Design workflows around draft creation + human send; pull attachments via Drive instead.

mistakes.title: Treating the connector default posture as locked down
mistakes.body: The default enterprise posture is open: users can enable catalog connectors without approval unless admins restrict them (Harmonic Security, 2026-03-10).
mistakes.fix: Set org-level connector policies (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked) and deploy `managed-mcp.json` allowlists.

mistakes.title: Connecting a localhost or VPN-only MCP server
mistakes.body: Remote connectors are reached from Anthropic's cloud, not your machine; servers behind VPNs, firewalls, private DNS, or IP allowlists will fail (Sunpeak, 2026-07-29).
mistakes.fix: Expose a public HTTPS endpoint (tunnel for dev) or use desktop extensions/local MCP.

mistakes.title: Granting broad OAuth scopes out of convenience
mistakes.body: MCP security guidance: minimum-necessary grants, prefer read-only, treat third-party tool descriptions as untrusted (MCP security best practices; OWASP MCP Top 10).
mistakes.fix: Scope OAuth grants tightly at consent time and prefer read-only tool sets.

mistakes.title: Trusting directory listing as a security guarantee
mistakes.body: Anthropic reviews submissions against the MCP Directory Policy, but a listing is not a guarantee of security, uptime, or tool quality; review is human and queue-based (Directory FAQ; MCP registry guidance).
mistakes.fix: Vet third-party connectors yourself; pin versions and re-review on updates ("rug pull" risk is documented).

mistakes.title: Expecting custom connectors to work in scheduled routines
mistakes.body: A documented gap: custom MCP connectors cannot be attached to scheduled routines (no UUID discovery path — claude-code issue #63233, May 2026).
mistakes.fix: Use first-party connectors in routines, or run connector-dependent automations interactively until this ships.

mistakes.title: Forwarding tokens across servers (token passthrough)
mistakes.body: Passing a token issued for one server to another is an explicitly forbidden anti-pattern in the MCP spec (MCP security best practices).
mistakes.fix: Validate token audience per server; issue separate tokens per resource.

mistakes.title: Assuming web search respects egress controls
mistakes.body: Web search is a built-in Anthropic-managed capability (not a connector), and in Cowork it bypasses network egress restrictions (Harmonic Security, 2026-03-10); MCP connections also bypass code-execution egress settings (support.claude.com).
mistakes.fix: Treat web search and MCP as separate exfiltration paths in your threat model.

mistakes.title: Assuming every connector writes as well as reads
mistakes.body: Write surfaces vary and shift: Notion and Google connectors were read/create-only in early 2026 with write support expanding mid-year (conflicting sources — flagged); Teams remains read-only in the M365 connector (2026-07-07 release notes).
mistakes.fix: Verify the current tool list per connector before promising write workflows.

mistakes.title: Running `bypassPermissions` outside a container
mistakes.body: Anthropic documents `--dangerously-skip-permissions`/bypassPermissions as for "isolated environments like containers or VMs" only (Claude Code — Configure permissions).
mistakes.fix: Use `acceptEdits` or `auto` mode interactively; reserve bypass for sandboxed CI.

mistakes.title: Not understanding permission-mode semantics
mistakes.body: Six modes exist (default/Manual, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions) with deny → ask → allow rule precedence, and rules are enforced by Claude Code, not the model (Claude Code docs).
mistakes.fix: Learn the modes (Shift+Tab cycles them) and encode rules in settings rather than re-answering prompts.

mistakes.title: Over-specified CLAUDE.md files
mistakes.body: Anthropic lists "over-specified CLAUDE.md" as a failure pattern and targets under 200 lines: longer files consume context and reduce adherence (Claude Code — Memory/best practices).
mistakes.fix: Keep CLAUDE.md concise; move path-specific rules into `.claude/rules/*.md` with `paths:` frontmatter.

mistakes.title: Writing instructions in AGENTS.md expecting Claude Code to read them
mistakes.body: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md (Claude Code — Memory).
mistakes.fix: Create a CLAUDE.md that imports your AGENTS.md via `@path/to/import` syntax.

mistakes.title: Treating the Bash sandbox as a complete security boundary
mistakes.body: Documented limitations: no TLS inspection by default, Unix-socket escalation paths, "not a complete isolation boundary"; native Windows is unsupported (Claude Code — Sandboxing).
mistakes.fix: Combine sandboxing with permission rules and managed enforcement (`failIfUnavailable`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`).

mistakes.title: The kitchen-sink session
mistakes.body: Anthropic's documented failure patterns include mega-sessions that mix unrelated tasks and "correcting over and over" (Claude Code — Best practices).
mistakes.fix: `/clear` between tasks; after two failed corrections, restart with a sharper prompt.

mistakes.title: No verification loop
mistakes.body: "Give Claude a way to verify its work… the single highest-leverage thing you can do" (Claude Code — Best practices).
mistakes.fix: Provide tests, linters, or screenshot checks so Claude can confirm changes against the running app.

mistakes.title: Surprise at cost and rate-limit windows
mistakes.body: Claude Code draws from a per-seat allowance on rolling 5-hour and weekly windows shared with chat and Cowork; API-billed usage averages ~$13/developer/active day (Claude Code — Manage costs).
mistakes.fix: Monitor with `/usage`; route routine tasks to cheaper models via subagents; set `--max-budget-usd` in automation.

mistakes.title: Assuming cloud sessions work with your org's IP allowlist
mistakes.body: Claude Code on the web shares account rate limits and org IP allowlists break cloud sessions; it is also unavailable on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry (Claude Code on the web docs).
mistakes.fix: Check infrastructure constraints before adopting `--cloud` workflows.

mistakes.title: Assuming there's a repo index
mistakes.body: There is no separate indexing step; Claude Code explores agentically at query time (Glob/Grep/Read + Explore subagent), guided by CLAUDE.md (Claude Code docs).
mistakes.fix: Invest in a good CLAUDE.md and clear code layout instead of waiting for an "indexing" to finish.

mistakes.title: Confusing audit logs with the Compliance API
mistakes.body: Audit logs (Enterprise-only, 180 days) are metadata-only: chat/project titles and content are NOT included, only UUIDs; full content requires the Compliance API (Admin API keys with `read:compliance_activities`) or Primary-Owner data exports (Anthropic audit-log docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Use audit logs for who/when/what-event; Compliance API for content investigations.

mistakes.title: Assuming Cowork sessions are audited
mistakes.body: A reported gap: Cowork sessions are not captured in audit logs/compliance data (claudeforoperators, May 2026 — Medium confidence; may have changed since Cowork GA).
mistakes.fix: Verify current Cowork audit coverage with Anthropic before relying on logs for Cowork oversight.

mistakes.title: Assuming ZDR covers everything
mistakes.body: Zero Data Retention covers the Messages API and Token Counting API but EXCLUDES Batch API, Files API, Skills API, code execution, programmatic tool calling, MCP connectors, and Console/Workbench; Covered Models (Fable 5, Mythos 5) require 30-day retention and are incompatible with ZDR-only workspaces (Anthropic ZDR docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Map each workload against the ZDR scope list before claiming zero retention.

mistakes.title: Routing PHI through non-eligible features
mistakes.body: Under a BAA, HIPAA covers the Messages API plus specified tools/APIs but NOT Console/Workbench, Free/Pro/Max/Team, Cowork, Batch/Files/Skills APIs, Code Execution, Computer Use, Web Fetch, or betas (privacy.claude.com — BAA for Commercial Customers, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Restrict PHI workflows to HIPAA-eligible surfaces; note Claude Code CLI is covered only with ZDR enabled.

mistakes.title: Enabling HIPAA on self-serve Enterprise
mistakes.body: The HIPAA-ready configuration is available on sales-assisted Enterprise (and legacy/AWS Marketplace SKUs); self-serve Enterprise cannot enable it in-app (Anthropic Enterprise FAQ, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Engage Anthropic sales for a BAA-backed HIPAA configuration.

mistakes.title: Quoting stale API retention defaults
mistakes.body: API inputs/outputs default to 7-day retention (reduced from 30 days on 2025-09-14), with 30-day retention available via DPA opt-in (Anthropic policy — flagged as repeatedly changed).
mistakes.fix: Verify the current retention article; opt in via the DPA if your compliance posture needs 30 days.

mistakes.title: Assuming consumer data policies apply to Enterprise
mistakes.body: On commercial products (Team/Enterprise/API) prompts and results are NOT used for training by default — contractual, with no opt-in/opt-out toggle, unlike consumer tiers post-Sept 2025 (Anthropic Enterprise page).
mistakes.fix: State the commercial default correctly in internal privacy reviews; don't extrapolate consumer-policy news to Enterprise.

mistakes.title: Expecting EU data residency on first-party surfaces
mistakes.body: EU residency is not offered on claude.ai or the direct API; EU paths exist only via AWS Bedrock EU profiles or Google Vertex AI EU regions (Anthropic residency docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Route EU-residency requirements through Bedrock/Vertex under the cloud provider's DPA.

mistakes.title: Underestimating shared-chat and published-artifact exposure
mistakes.body: The July 2026 indexing incident showed shared chats/artifacts becoming Google-indexed; share links have no per-viewer auth (TechCrunch, 2026-07-27).
mistakes.fix: Set an org policy for public sharing, audit links regularly, and prefer project-scoped sharing with View/Edit permissions.

mistakes.title: Skipping spend controls until the invoice arrives
mistakes.body: Enterprise offers org- and user-level spend limits with alerts (reported at 75%/90% thresholds — single secondary source, flagged) plus usage analytics; self-serve draws from a shared prepaid credit pool that stops org-wide at zero (Anthropic, Jul 2026).
mistakes.fix: Configure spend limits and alerts at rollout, not after the first surprise bill.

mistakes.title: Treating 429 and 529 the same
mistakes.body: 429 `rate_limit_error` is your problem (requests too fast — respect `retry-after`); 529 `overloaded_error` is Anthropic-wide capacity (retry with capped exponential backoff + jitter) (Anthropic error docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Branch your retry logic on error type and headers, not just "any failure → retry."

mistakes.title: Status-code-only error handling on streams
mistakes.body: Streaming connections open with HTTP 200 and can deliver `overloaded_error` as an in-stream error event; status-code checks alone miss it (documented streaming behavior).
mistakes.fix: Parse stream events for error types and handle mid-stream failures.

mistakes.title: Caching misuse — mutating the prefix
mistakes.body: Prompt-cache invalidation follows a hierarchy (tools → system → messages); any byte change in a prefix invalidates everything after it (Anthropic — Prompt caching).
mistakes.fix: Put stable content first, volatile content last, and place `cache_control` breakpoints deliberately (max 4 per request).

mistakes.title: Assuming cache TTL and minimums are universal
mistakes.body: Default TTL is 5 minutes (1-hour option at 2× write cost), minimum cacheable prefix varies by model (e.g., 1,024 tokens Sonnet 4.5/4.6; 4,096 Haiku 4.5), and Claude Code cache lifetime is an hour on subscription vs five minutes on API keys (Anthropic docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Check per-model minimums and choose TTL per workload; cache reads cost 0.1× input.

mistakes.title: Sending `Authorization: Bearer` with an API key
mistakes.body: API keys authenticate via the `x-api-key` header (bearer is for short-lived OAuth/Workload Identity tokens), plus required `anthropic-version` (Anthropic authentication docs).
mistakes.fix: Use `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version` headers; store the key as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

mistakes.title: Returning `tool_result` for server-side tools
mistakes.body: Server tools (web search, code execution) use `srvtoolu_` IDs and execute on Anthropic infrastructure; never send `tool_result` for them (Anthropic API docs).
mistakes.fix: Only return tool results for client-side tools (`toolu_` IDs) your application executes.

mistakes.title: Ignoring new stop reasons
mistakes.body: `pause_turn` (long multi-search requests) and `model_context_window_exceeded` are documented stop reasons that naive completion checks miss (Anthropic API docs, 2026).
mistakes.fix: Handle all stop reasons explicitly; continue on `pause_turn` instead of assuming the turn ended.

mistakes.title: Expecting streaming or speed from the Batch API
mistakes.body: Message Batches are asynchronous (results within 24h, most <1h), 50% cheaper, retained 29 days, no streaming, and not available on Claude Platform on AWS (Anthropic — Batch API).
mistakes.fix: Use Batch for offline bulk jobs; use the streaming Messages API for interactive latency.

mistakes.title: Assuming Files API uploads are downloadable and covered by ZDR
mistakes.body: Uploaded files cannot be re-downloaded (only files Claude creates can be), files persist until explicitly deleted (an exception to auto-deletion), and the Files API is excluded from ZDR (Anthropic — Files API beta; ZDR scope).
mistakes.fix: Keep source copies locally; delete files explicitly; exclude Files API flows from ZDR-scoped pipelines.

mistakes.title: Building agent frameworks before exhausting simple patterns
mistakes.body: Anthropic's own guidance: "find the simplest solution possible… this might mean not building agentic systems at all"; agents cost ~4× and multi-agent ~15× the tokens of chat, and errors compound in sandboxes (Anthropic Engineering — Building effective agents; multi-agent research system).
mistakes.fix: Start with prompt chaining, routing, or a single augmented LLM; graduate to orchestrator-workers or autonomous agents only when measured need exists.
